alantos-pharmaceuticals-ag.name: Alantos Pharmaceuticals

entry.quote: Earlybird hat sich im Februar 2003 als Co-Lead Investor in der Series C Runde beteiligt.
entry.entry_asserted: Firm's own exit release (06.06.2007) dates Earlybird's participation to the Series C in February 2003 and names no earlier Earlybird round; the firm's 18.07.2003 release announces the same EUR 24.1M round (led by Oxford Bioscience, Earlybird 'local co-lead') together with the rename from Therascope AG.

rounds.round: Series C (announced as 'second round of institutional preferred stock financing')

alantos-pharmaceuticals-ag.status_detail: Amgen agreed to acquire Alantos Pharmaceuticals Holding, Inc. for USD 300M in cash (announced 2007-06-06).

valuation.basis: signed acquisition price (cash), below $1B

alantos-pharmaceuticals-ag.notes: Small-molecule drug discovery (DPP-IV inhibitor for type 2 diabetes), founded in Heidelberg as Therascope AG; renamed Alantos in 2003; HQ moved from Heidelberg to Cambridge, Massachusetts in 2005 (firm release 605). Earlybird III portfolio company. The firm's February 2003 date and the July 2003 announcement refer to the same round.

amaxa-gmbh.name: amaxa

entry.round: First financing round (the firm does not name it Seed or Series A; it calls itself 'Startphasen-Investor')
entry.quote: stellte Ende November 1998 auch die erste Finanzierungsrunde von Amaxa
entry.entry_asserted: Firm release of 27.05.2008 says Earlybird found amaxa in the 1998 NUK business-plan competition and provided its first financing round at the end of November 1998; the founder calls Earlybird 'Amaxas ersten Investor'.

rounds.round: second financing round (3i and TMK joined)

graduation.later_round: second financing round (unnamed, no amount in the record)
graduation.quote: In einer zweiten Finanzierungsrunde im Mai 2001 kamen die Investoren 3i und TMK dazu.
graduation.note: The later round is real and first-party, but the record neither names it Series A nor states an amount.

amaxa-gmbh.status_detail: Lonza Group agreed to acquire amaxa AG with all its activities (announced 2008-05-27, price undisclosed; closing expected early Q3 2008). The German register now shows amaxa AG as Lonza Cologne GmbH.

valuation.basis: price undisclosed; press estimate CHF 100-200M (fuw.ch headline), no figure of $1B or more

amaxa-gmbh.notes: Non-viral gene transfer (Nucleofector) products for cell research, Cologne, founded 1998. Earlybird's first-fund investment; the April 1999 firm release already lists 'Amaxa GmbH, Köln' among new holdings. The entry round is the company's first round but the firm never labels it Seed or Series A.

bmeye.name: BMEYE

entry.quote: New investors Earlybird, who led this round, and 360 Capital Partners participated in the financing
entry.entry_asserted: Company release calls Earlybird a new investor in the Series B; the 2006 Series A was led by LSP. Firm archive first lists Bmeye as a recent investment in 2009-10.

bmeye.status_detail: Edwards Lifesciences completed the acquisition of BMEYE B.V. for EUR 32.5M (about USD 42M), announced 2012-10-10.

valuation.basis: signed acquisition price, below $1B

bmeye.notes: Non-invasive continuous blood-pressure and cardiac-output monitoring (Nexfin), Amsterdam. Earlybird IV investment.

zonare-medical-systems.name: ZONARE Medical Systems (formerly NovaSonics)

entry.quote: both of Novasonics' Series B investors, Earlybird, and Frazier Healthcare, are participants in the Series C funding round
entry.entry_asserted: The Nov 2001 Series C release (on the firm's site) names Earlybird and Frazier as the two Series B investors; the S-1/A dates the Series B to September 2000 at USD 9M and the Series A (USD 2M, 1999 to Jan 2000) has no Earlybird record. The firm's March 2001 release lists Novasonics among Earlybird III's first holdings. Caveat: the firm's 2004 release loosely calls Earlybird 'einer der Erstrundeninvestoren'.

rounds.amount_native: USD 34M in closings Sep 2001 to Aug 2002 (USD 21.5M announced Nov 2001)

zonare-medical-systems.status_detail: Mindray Medical International completed the acquisition of ZONARE Medical Systems for USD 101.7M in cash on 2013-07-17 (agreement of 2013-06-12). The 2008 Nasdaq IPO filing never priced.

valuation.basis: signed acquisition price, below $1B

zonare-medical-systems.notes: Compact premium ultrasound systems; incorporated April 1999 as NovaSonics, renamed ZONARE in October 2002. Holder of record is Earlybird Verwaltung GmbH as trustee for the Earlybird III funds (13.9% before the planned IPO). The pipeline's prepared entry (Series A, 2009, from a Form D band) is wrong: the 2009 and 2010 Form Ds are late rounds; Earlybird's first round is the September 2000 Series B.

noemalife.name: NoemaLife

rounds.round: first round of venture financing in GMD Gesellschaft fuer Medizinische Datenverarbeitung mbH (Cologne), not in NoemaLife
IPO (Borsa Italiana, Expandi segment, first trading day 2006-05-10)

noemalife.status_detail: Dedalus S.p.A. bought control of NoemaLife in June 2016 (100% of Ghenos, the founder's holding with 57.3%, plus the Tamburi and Maggioli stakes), then launched a mandatory tender offer at EUR 7.40 per share aimed at delisting.

valuation.basis: small-cap listing; tender offer at EUR 7.40 per share, no figure of $1B or more

noemalife.membership_detail: Earlybird financed GMD Gesellschaft fuer Medizinische Datenverarbeitung (Cologne) in 1999; GMD merged in 2002 with NoemaLife's predecessor and Earlybird's NoemaLife shares came from that merger. The firm's own release (16.05.2006) describes only this path: 'In 1999, Earlybird provided a first round of Venture financing to GMD ... In 2002 the company merged with NoemaLife's predecessor.' No record of new Earlybird money into NoemaLife was found: the firm press archive 2001 to 2010 was read for every NoemaLife mention, and Bing News '"NoemaLife" Earlybird' returns only Medasys and Dedalus items that do not name Earlybird.
noemalife.notes: Clinical and laboratory information software for hospitals, Bologna; listed in Milan in May 2006. Earlybird's position is the merger consideration for GMD, which is its own row; the firm counts NoemaLife as a first-fund IPO exit.

calypso-medical.name: Calypso Medical Technologies

rounds.round: Series A (vendor label; first institutional round, 'Biotech lands $8.5 million to develop tumor tracker')

rounds.lead: Skyline Ventures and Frazier Healthcare Ventures

calypso-medical.status_detail: Varian Medical Systems acquired Calypso Medical Technologies in October 2011 for USD 10M plus contingent consideration (agreement announced 2011-09-19).

valuation.basis: signed acquisition price (Varian 10-K), below $1B

calypso-medical.notes: Real-time tumor tracking ('GPS for the body') for radiotherapy, Seattle. Earlybird's round is not named in any page that loads: the firm's 07.03.2001 release lists Calypso among the first 14 Earlybird III holdings (so the entry falls between August 2000 and February 2001), and its 2002 and 2004 releases list it as a current holding. Vendor data (PitchBook, via search summary) puts an USD 8.5M Series A at September 2000 and an USD 25.3M Series B at May 2002, which would make the entry the 2000 Series A, but no loadable first-party or press page ties Earlybird to it (fdanews item 69248 is gone; EDGAR holds only Form D / REGDEX notices, no prospectus). Entry left null. Searched: firm press archive; Bing News '"Calypso Medical" Earlybird', '"Calypso Medical" "Series B"', '"Calypso Medical Technologies" financing' (0 items each); two web searches.

entelos-inc.name: Entelos

entry.quote: raised $25 million in a private financing led by Bear Stearns Health Innoventures. Other investors included Earlybird
entry.entry_asserted: The firm's 05.02.2002 release says its Entelos investment was made in 2001 ('In 2001, we demonstrated this commitment with investments in Entelos'); the September 2001 USD 25M financing is the only 2001 round and names Earlybird. The loaded snippet calls it a 'private financing'; a search summary of the PE Week Wire of 2001-09-06 calls it a Series C with Earlybird as a new investor, but that page is behind registration, so the round name is left null.

rounds.round: private financing (reported as Series C, unverified)
IPO on AIM, London (ENTL), first trading day 2006-04-12

entelos-inc.status_detail: Entelos, Inc. went through Chapter 11; substantially all of its assets were sold in a Section 363 auction on 2011-09-21 (US Bankruptcy Court, District of Delaware). Simulations Plus was only the backup bidder; the business continued as Entelos Holding Corp. under its lender Imperium, and Clearlake Capital took a majority stake in January 2012 (WSJ and PE Hub headlines).

valuation.basis: bankruptcy asset sale; the backup bid was USD 1.85M; AIM small cap before that

entelos-inc.notes: Predictive biosimulation ('virtual patients', PhysioLab) for drug R&D; Menlo Park at the time of Earlybird's investment, Foster City in the firm's 2006 to 2008 releases. The firm counts Entelos in its second fund generation (Earlybird III); AIM listing in April 2006, Chapter 11 in 2011 with a Section 363 asset sale, so the row reads acquired (successor Entelos Holding Corp.). Round name unverified: null rather than a guess.

wilex-ag.name: Wilex (now Heidelberg Pharma AG)

entry.round: Series A (the firm calls it the 'A1-Investorenrunde')
entry.quote: beteiligte sich daraufhin mit der A1–Investorenrunde im März 1999
entry.entry_asserted: Firm's IPO release (13.11.2006) says Earlybird introduced Sven Warnaar to the CEO and 'thereupon' invested with the A1 investor round in March 1999; Wilex was founded in September 1997 and no earlier Earlybird round is named.

rounds.round: IPO, Frankfurt Prime Standard (WL6), issue price EUR 13.80

wilex-ag.status_detail: Listed in Frankfurt since November 2006; renamed Heidelberg Pharma AG in October 2017 (ticker HPHA, Xetra / Frankfurt Prime Standard). Market cap EUR 109.94M on 2026-10-06 (about USD 0.12B).

valuation.basis: market cap read from stockanalysis.com (Xetra: HPHA); companiesmarketcap.com shows USD 0.12B as of October 2026

wilex-ag.notes: Oncology biotech founded in Munich in 1997 by physicians and cancer researchers of TU München (antibody Rencarex, uPA inhibitors). Now Heidelberg Pharma AG, seated in Ladenburg: 'formerly known as Wilex AG and changed its name to Heidelberg Pharma AG in October 2017' (stockanalysis.com company page). Earlybird's entry is the March 1999 A1 round; its 07.03.2001 release also lists Wilex among Earlybird III holdings (a follow-on), and the firm 'remains invested' at the IPO.

perfuze.name: Perfuze

entry.quote: The funding round was led by Earlybird Venture Capital
entry.entry_asserted: Irish Times (2019-01-29): Perfuze, founded 2018, 'has closed a €3 million seed investment'; the CEO calls it 'our seed round financing'. The firm lists the investment year as 2018 (close year), and the 2022 Series A names Earlybird as an existing investor.

rounds.lead: existing investors incl. Earlybird, EQT Life Sciences, Seroba, SV Health

graduation.quote: Perfuze has raised €22.5m in a Series A funding round to push forward with clinical studies

perfuze.status_detail: Operating; EUR 22M follow-on in March 2025 and pivotal MARRS trial results announced in August 2026.

valuation.basis: no priced figure of $1B or more; total raised about EUR 50M

perfuze.notes: Catheter-based aspiration technology (Millipede, Zipline) for acute ischemic stroke; Earlybird Health led the seed. The firm list's 'Seed' label is right here.

alesi-surgical.name: Alesi Surgical

entry.lead: Panakes Partners and Earlybird (the two new investors)
entry.quote: The new investment comes from two leading med tech European venture capital firms, Panakes Partners and Earlybird Venture Capital
entry.entry_asserted: Company release (reproduced by Talent4Boards and MediWales, June 2017): Earlybird and Panakes are the new investors, IP Group and Finance Wales the existing ones; Thom Rasche joins the board 'as part of the investment'. The firm lists the investment year as 2017. The release does not name the round ('raised a further €6m'); the firm list's 'Series B' is not confirmed by any page.

rounds.source: Google News headline, Insider Media 2015-03-30: 'Alesi Surgical secures £2.1m investment'

rounds.round: funding round (unnamed in the release; the publisher tags it Series B)

alesi-surgical.status_detail: Active at Companies House (No. 06133243, Cardiff Medicentre); closed a GBP 7M round led by IW Capital in April 2026.

valuation.basis: no priced figure of $1B or more; over GBP 21M raised in total by 2024 (Mercia)

alesi-surgical.notes: Cardiff University spin-out (formerly Asalus Medical Instruments, founded 2009) whose Ultravision system clears surgical smoke by electrostatic precipitation. Earlybird Health entered in the June 2017 round as a new investor. The 2024 and 2026 releases name IP Group, Panakes and Mercia as existing investors and do not name Earlybird, though the firm's site still lists the company as active with a board observer.

atlantic-therapeutics.name: Atlantic Therapeutics

entry.quote: has raised €15 million in funding from investors, including Seroba Life Sciences and Earlybird Venture Capital
entry.entry_asserted: Irish Times (2017-03-01): first outside funding of the Bio-Medical Research spin-out; Thom Rasche of Earlybird joins the board with this round. The article does not name the round. The next round (January 2019, EUR 28M, led by LSP) is named Series B and describes Seroba and Earlybird as having 'previously invested', so the 2017 round is the first institutional round, but no loaded page calls it Series A: round left null.

rounds.amount_native: EUR 15M (plus loan capital from Silicon Valley Bank)

atlantic-therapeutics.status_detail: Acquired by Caldera Medical (US) for an undisclosed sum, reported 2023-09-07 (not 2021).

valuation.basis: acquisition price undisclosed; no figure of $1B or more

atlantic-therapeutics.notes: Maker of the Innovo wearable pelvic-floor stimulator for stress urinary incontinence; spun out of Bio-Medical Research Group, Galway. The 2019 round is named 'Series B' in the FinSMEs headline ('Atlantic Therapeutics Raises €28M in Series B Funding'); Galway Daily gives the investors.

polares-medical.name: Polares Medical

entry.quote: Polares Medical closed a $25 million Series A financing in 2018
entry.entry_asserted: The July 2018 release names the investors of the USD 25M round: 'led by Decheng Capital ... together with Endeavour Vision (Geneva), IDO Investments (Muscat), Earlybird Venture Capital (Berlin) and Wellington Partners' (startupticker.ch, 18.07.2018); the June 2020 release calls that round the Series A. Polares was spun off from Symetis in 2017, so there is no earlier round.

polares-medical.status_detail: Operating, clinical stage; closed a USD 50M Series C in March 2026.

valuation.basis: no priced figure of $1B or more; about USD 115M raised in total

polares-medical.notes: Transcatheter posterior-leaflet (hemi-valve) replacement for mitral regurgitation; Symetis spin-off with offices in Lausanne and Palo Alto. The firm list's 'Series B' label is wrong for the entry: Earlybird was already in the 2018 Series A and followed on in the 2020 Series B.

istar-medical.name: iSTAR Medical

entry.quote: The financing was led by healthcare specialist funds LSP and Gimv, with participation by Earlybird and BNP Paribas Fortis Private Equity.
entry.entry_asserted: Company release (2019-09-05) lists Earlybird among the new investors ('We are delighted to welcome LSP, Gimv, Earlybird and BNP Paribas Fortis Private Equity to iSTAR Medical') apart from the 'existing shareholders'; Lionel Carnot (Earlybird) joins the board with the round. The firm gives 2019 as the investment year.

rounds.round: non-dilutive upfront payment from AbbVie with an exclusive right to acquire

istar-medical.status_detail: Independent. AbbVie paid USD 60M upfront in July 2022 for an exclusive right to acquire iSTAR (up to USD 475M in closing and milestone payments); no exercise has been announced and the Belgian register shows Istar Medical N.V., Wavre, without a dissolution or bankruptcy mark.

valuation.basis: option terms only: USD 60M upfront plus up to USD 475M contingent; no figure of $1B or more

istar-medical.notes: Glaucoma micro-implant (MINIject, supraciliary MIGS device), Wavre, Belgium, founded 2011. The firm list's 'Pre-Seed' label is wrong: Earlybird Health entered at the EUR 40M Series C. An acquisition option is not an acquisition; the newest company release is from April 2025.

oviva.name: Oviva

entry.quote: Leading the round is MTIP, with participation by new investor Earlybird and existing investors AlbionVC, F-Prime Capital, Eight Roads Ventures and Partech.
entry.entry_asserted: TechCrunch (2020-01-14) and the company release (Moneycab copy: 'Auch Earlybird ist als neuer Investor dabei') both call Earlybird a new investor in the Series B. The firm's 'Invested 2019' is the close year.

oviva.status_detail: Operating; closed a USD 220M Series D led by Kinnevik (USD 100M, now the largest shareholder) in January 2026.

valuation.basis: no valuation is stated in the Series D coverage read (startupticker.ch, Kinnevik release via finanznachrichten.de); the round was part secondary. Worth a check of Kinnevik's quarterly report for a stated value before this is final.

oviva.notes: Digital dietary and behaviour-change therapy for obesity and type 2 diabetes, reimbursed by health systems in Germany, the UK and Switzerland. Registered seat is Oviva AG, Altendorf (canton Schwyz); the firm's page says Zurich and the 2020 release is datelined Zurich. The firm's 'Series B' label is right. Valuation is the open point: a USD 220M round with no stated figure.

sense-biodetection.name: Sense Biodetection

entry.amount: GBP 10.5M (GBP 12.3M with a GBP 1.8M Innovate UK grant)
entry.quote: The company has raised £10.5m Series A investment co-led by Cambridge Innovation Capital (CIC) and Earlybird
entry.entry_asserted: Company release (2019-10-29) names Earlybird a co-lead of the Series A and sets it apart from 'seed round investor Mercia Asset Management', so Earlybird was not in the seed. The firm gives 2019 as the investment year.

rounds.round: Series B (USD 50M earlier in 2021 plus a USD 15M extension)

sense-biodetection.status_detail: Sherlock Biosciences announced the acquisition of Sense Biodetection on 2023-02-01; terms not disclosed. It was a sale, not an administration: Sense Biodetection Limited (Companies House 08624309, Abingdon) is still an active company.

valuation.basis: acquisition terms undisclosed; no figure of $1B or more

sense-biodetection.notes: Instrument-free, disposable molecular diagnostic tests (Veros COVID-19), founded 2014 by Harry and Ralph Lamble. The 2019 release is datelined Cambridge; the registered office and the later press ('Abingdon, England-based', BioWorld 2021) give Abingdon. The Series B line rests on the BioWorld headline and snippet seen through Bing News (the page itself sits behind a bot wall).

oculis.name: Oculis

entry.round: Series B (preferred Series B shares issued in March 2020, the last B2 tranche)
entry.quote: In March 2020, we issued preferred Series B shares to fund research and development activities and general working capital.
entry.entry_asserted: No page names Earlybird's first round in words. Three facts fix it: the firm dates its investment 2020 and labels it Series B; the May 2021 Series C release lists 'EarlyBird' among 'the company's existing investors'; and the F-4 shows a single share issue in 2020, the March 2020 preferred Series B issue (CHF 5.0M proceeds). The F-4 share table splits Series B2 into three tranches (T1 to T3).

rounds.round: Nasdaq listing by merger with European Biotech Acquisition Corp. plus PIPE of about USD 91M (funds managed by Earlybird took part)

oculis.status_detail: Nasdaq: OCS (Oculis Holding AG) since 2023-03-03, after the business combination with European Biotech Acquisition Corp. Market cap USD 535.22M on 2026-10-06.

valuation.basis: current market cap (stockanalysis.com; companiesmarketcap.com shows USD 0.53B for 2026-10-06). The same companiesmarketcap page lists a year-end 2025 market cap of USD 1.18B, so the company was above $1B at the end of 2025 and has fallen back since; the judge should decide which date the band follows.

oculis.notes: Ophthalmology biopharma developing topical eye-drug formulations (candidates for retinal and neuro-ophthalmic disease); the technology comes from University of Iceland researchers, which is why Wikidata gives IS. Registered seat of Oculis Holding AG is Zug (stockanalysis.com company page, Swiss register); the firm's page and the company's releases are datelined Lausanne. The prepared country IS is wrong: CH. The entry is not post-IPO: Earlybird held preferred shares three years before the listing. Earlybird Growth GmbH is also a party to the October 2022 convertible loan agreement (F-4).

priothera.name: Priothera

entry.quote: with participation from co-lead investor HealthCap and funds managed by Tekla Capital Management as well as Earlybird Venture Capital
entry.entry_asserted: Silicon Republic (2020-10-12): Priothera 'has raised €30m in Series A funding'; the company was founded in 2020 and this is its first round; Lionel Carnot of Earlybird joins the board with it. The firm's 'Series A' label is right.

rounds.round: Series B (being raised: target EUR 40M, EUR 15M still missing in July 2025)

priothera.status_detail: Operating, phase 3 (MO-TRANS study of mocravimod in AML); EUR 63M raised since 2020 in equity and non-dilutive loans, Series B in progress in July 2025.

valuation.basis: no priced figure; the French article's word 'licorne' comes with no valuation and is not usable

priothera.notes: Clinical-stage company developing mocravimod (S1P receptor modulator) for AML patients receiving stem-cell transplants; seat in Dublin, operations in Saint-Louis (Haut-Rhin, France). Its CEO and co-founder Florent Gros became Venture Partner of Earlybird's Health Fund II in 2022 (Oculis F-4), two years after Earlybird's fund invested in the Series A.

arga-medtech.name: Argá Medtech

entry.quote: The round was led by the existing investors, Advent Life Sciences (UK) and Earlybird Health (Germany)
entry.entry_asserted: The February 2024 Series B release calls Earlybird Health an existing investor; the company was co-founded in June 2020 and the firm dates its investment 2021 (label 'Series A'), so Earlybird entered in the one round before the Series B. No loadable page names or sizes that round; vendor data (PitchBook, via a search summary) lists a Series A of USD 11.3M on 2021-01-21. Round left null because no first-party or press page names it.

rounds.round: Series A (vendor label, matches the firm's list)

rounds.lead: Advent Life Sciences and Earlybird Health, with Gilde Healthcare

arga-medtech.status_detail: Operating, clinical stage; first enrolments in the COHERENT-AF IDE trial announced September 2025 and BURST-AF first-in-human results reported February 2026 (headlines).

valuation.basis: no priced figure of $1B or more

arga-medtech.notes: Pulsed-field ablation system (Coherent Sine-Burst Electroporation) for atrial fibrillation; offices at the Biopôle campus and in San Diego. The Swiss register seat is Arga Medtech SA, Epalinges (the Biopôle municipality); the company and the firm write Lausanne. Earlybird Health co-led the Series B as an existing investor. Searched for the first round: Bing and Google News '"Argá Medtech" Series A', '"Arga Medtech" 2021 Advent Life Sciences financing' (nothing before 2022); ggba.swiss, bioalps.org and startupticker.ch pages (Series B only); one web search.

noscendo.name: Noscendo

entry.quote: Auch die Bestands-Investoren Earlybird Health, Wieland Capital, Paua Ventures und High-Tech Gründerfonds (HTGF) sollen sich erneut beteiligt haben.
entry.entry_asserted: Earlybird Health is an existing investor at the May 2022 Series B (startbase, loaded) and is absent from the December 2018 round (HTGF release: Wieland Capital as lead, HTGF, three business angels). The one round in between is the Series A of April 2020 (headlines: BioWorld 2020-04-26 'Noscendo closes series A round for rapid bloodstream infection diagnostic test'; FinSMEs 2020-04-23 'Noscendo Raises Series A Funding'), and the firm dates its investment 2020. Both 2020 pages sit behind bot walls, so the Series A name rests on their headlines and on the next round being the Series B; the register shows the matching capital increase (shareholder agreement 2020-02-19, capital EUR 68,916 on 2020-03-16).

rounds.lead: Revent and an unnamed family office (new investors)

noscendo.status_detail: Insolvency filed at the end of March 2026 (Duisburg Local Court, 620 IN 682/26; provisional administrator appointed 2026-03-30) after a failed financing round. In July 2026 Bruker took over the DISQVER platform and selected assets of the insolvent Noscendo GmbH in an asset deal ('übertragene Sanierung'). Insolvency followed by an asset sale: acquired, successor Bruker.

valuation.basis: asset sale out of insolvency, price undisclosed; about EUR 27M (deutsche-startups.de) to almost EUR 40M (Unternehmeredition) of venture capital raised in total

noscendo.notes: Software-based pathogen identification from blood by next-generation sequencing (DISQVER test). Register: Noscendo GmbH, Duisburg, in liquidation since 2026-06-17 (North Data). deutsche-startups.de (2026-07-24): 'Bruker übernimmt das insolvente Duisburger MedTech-Unternehmen Noscendo' and names Earlybird among the investors.

wellabe.name: wellabe

entry.entry_asserted: Earlybird was already a shareholder when wellabe closed its Series A in December 2020 (tech.eu; Welt: 'neben den bisherigen Gesellschaftern Earlybird, Paua Ventures und Plug and Play'), so its entry is the earlier round. The firm dates it 2018 on its health site (2019 on the archived page) and labels it Pre-Seed; no loadable page names or sizes that round (vendor pages mention a EUR 1.8M seed). Round left null: it is a pre-Series-A round whose name the record does not give.

rounds.round: Seed (vendor label; the firm's list says Pre-Seed)

graduation.quote: Munich-based healthtech startup wellabe has closed a €3 million Series A round.

wellabe.status_detail: Mavie, an Austrian health-services provider, took a 60% majority stake in wellabe (announced 2024-08-28); the German register now carries the company as Mavie Work Deutschland GmbH, Munich. The firm's list marks it 'Exit'.

valuation.basis: price undisclosed; about EUR 5M raised in total (deutsche-startups.de)

wellabe.notes: Workplace health check-ups with a mobile lab plus digital prevention programmes (corporate health management), Munich, operating since 2018. Entry stage is pre-Series A by the record (existing investor at the Series A) but the round's own name is unverified; the Series A of December 2020 is the named later round. The archived firm page's description for this row is a copy error (it shows Workist's text).

Searched for a buyer of the assets: Bing and Google News (de) '"EBS Technologies" Eyetronic Insolvenz', '"Eyetronic" Therapie Glaukom 2019 OR 2020 OR 2021' (nothing).

miracor.name: Miracor Medical

Series D (final closing; first EUR 25M closed January 2018)

miracor.status_detail: Miracor Medical N.V./SA, Awans, Belgium, is on the Belgian register without a bankruptcy or dissolution mark and filed its annual report for 2025 on 2026-07-31; Thom Rasche (Earlybird) is listed as a director in the August 2023 filing. Earlybird IV holding since the 2008 Series A; the archived firm page's 'Invested in: 2016' is not the entry year. hemoteq-gmbh.name: Hemoteq

rounds.round: sale of 74.9% to Freudenberg Medical Europe (sellers include Pinova Capital and Earlybird)

hemoteq-gmbh.status_detail: Freudenberg Medical Europe bought 74.9% of Hemoteq AG in August 2015, price undisclosed; Earlybird and Pinova Capital were among the sellers. The register now carries the company as Freudenberg Medical Hemoteq GmbH, Würselen.

valuation.basis: price undisclosed; no figure of $1B or more

hemoteq-gmbh.notes: Surface coatings and drug-device combination products for medical devices (about 100 staff in 2015), Würselen near Aachen. Earlybird's round is not named anywhere that loads: the firm's 05.02.2002 release already lists Hemoteq among its life-science holdings and the 25.02.2004 release as a current medtech holding, so the entry is in early 2002 at the latest; LTO (2015) confirms Earlybird as a selling shareholder. Entry left null. The archived firm page's 'Acquired by BMC Software' for this row is a copy error (BMC bought Identify).
